title: Safe concurrent eviction with async checkpoints and tenant-aware GPU slab compaction
creator: Maya Patel
description: We need an eviction protocol that remains correct when multiple models/tenants concurrently access a shared GPU-resident KV cache while the system performs asynchronous checkpoints to persistent storage and background slab compaction. Current LRU/TTL-based evictions can drop entries that are still referenced by in-flight continuous batches or by a concurrent model rollout that expects a pinned prefix. This ticket designs, implements, and verifies a tenant-aware eviction fencing mechanism plus an async checkpoint fence so we can reclaim GPU memory safely and compact slabs without violating correctness or increasing tail latency.
background: Observations from recent incidents: (1) a model rollout that changed tokenizer boundaries caused prefix mismatches when KV entries were evicted during a live rollout; (2) slab compaction freed pages while an inflight batch tried to read KV pointers leading to transient invalid reads in native runtime (caught by ASAN in staging); (3) asynchronous checkpointing occasionally created race windows where a checkpointed state didn't include entries being re-inserted post-eviction. Existing tickets cover eviction invariants and lease-based approaches, but none address interaction with async checkpointing plus GPU slab compaction under continuous batching workloads.
proposed_solution: Introduce a three-part protocol: (1) Epoched eviction tokens per prefix: each prefix has a monotonically increasing epoch id. Writes/reads tag KV references with current epoch. (2) Eviction fencing via per-shard inflight lease counters: before freeing a slab or entry, the evictor increments a 'drain generation' and waits for inflight batch counters to drain below a safe threshold for that generation. New batches encountering a newer generation will conservatively re-pin entries. (3) Async checkpoint fence: checkpoints record the highest completed epoch per-prefix; eviction cannot permanently delete entries until a checkpoint has advanced past the entry's epoch OR the entry has been compacted with a transactional move that updates the checkpoint metadata. (4) Background slab compaction uses a buffer-swap technique: compaction builds a compacted slab in GPU memory, migrates live entries (honoring epoch tags and leases) and then atomically swaps slab pointers under the shard lock. This avoids pointer invalidation during compaction. Complement with GC sweep that respects epoch and checkpoint metadata. Also add telemetry for epoch/lease/generation metrics and a fail-open degraded mode that falls back to TTL-only eviction for low-memory emergencies.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests that simulate concurrent continuous batching with N=100 clients and 10 model rollouts show zero use-after-free or invalid reads in the runtime (ASAN/TSAN in CI)
End-to-end test where async checkpoint fails and recovers preserves KV correctness: no prefix mismatches after recovery
Measured overhead under 99th percentile latency: additional per-request CPU work < 150us and median latency increase < 5% for our 2kRPS benchmark
Slab compaction can reclaim >= 20% GPU memory under fragmentation workloads without any request errors during compaction
Fallback degraded mode triggers and recovers automatically when eviction fencing cannot wait (emergency reclaim) and is traceable in telemetry
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature flag gated rollout in staging with epoch/lease counters enabled for 10% of traffic; monitor correctness and latency
Phase 2: Increase to 50% traffic, enable slab compaction in dry-run (compaction prepares new slabs but does not swap them) to validate migration correctness
Phase 3: Enable atomic swap for compaction and async checkpoint fencing in canary region with SLO guardrails
Phase 4: Global rollout after 72 hours of clean metrics and sign-off from SRE/Runtime/PM
test_plan: Fuzz harness that injects eviction timing perturbations, checkpoint delays, and compaction pauses to reproduce race windows
Deterministic scenario runner that replays production batching traces with mixed model prefixes and asserts key liveness across epochs
ASAN/Valgrind CI jobs for native runtime changes triggered on PRs touching eviction/compaction code
Chaos test: randomly drop checkpoint writes and force emergency reclaim to verify degraded fallback path
Load test: 10k RPS mixed chat/generation workload measuring 50p/95p/99p latency and memory reclamation efficiency
monitoring: Telemetry: per-prefix epoch, per-shard drain-generation, inflight-lease-count gauge
Alert: drain-generation wait time exceeds threshold (configurable), triggers PagerDuty to SRE
Dashboards: compaction throughput, reclaimed bytes/sec, compaction swap latency histogram
SLO guard: 99th percentile request latency regression > 10% blocks rollout
Audit log: checkpoint fence events with epoch metadata for post-incident analysis
risks: Added metadata (epoch tags, lease counters) increases per-entry memory footprint on GPU; mitigated by compacted metadata packing and optional sampling for long-tail prefixes
Waiting for inflight drain could delay eviction and increase peak memory; mitigate with emergency reclaim fallback and configurable thresholds
Compaction swap introduces a short coordination lock that could add latency spikes; mitigation: do pointer swap under tiny critical section and pre-warm caches
Complexity increases attack surface for bugs in correctness protocol; mitigation: extensive deterministic tests, formal reasoning notes, and staged rollout
open_questions: What is the optimal size/type for the drain-generation wait window under our 95th percentile batch duration?
Should epoch counters be 32-bit or 64-bit to avoid wrap for long-running clusters?
Can we piggyback epoch metadata onto existing KV headers without rewriting on every entry update?
Do we need cross-shard two-phase commit for compaction when prefixes span shards?
